title: Elphie – Dental Imaging Capture and Live Streaming
summary: A dental imaging system pairing a C++ application that drives an intraoral camera and detects caries with a web application I built from scratch for recorded video, live streaming, appointments, and diagnoses.
role: Cloud video, live streaming, and web application development
overview: Elphie combines a C++ desktop application and a web application. The C++ side controls an external intraoral camera, takes its feed, and runs a model that detects caries while the dentist examines the patient.
My contribution was everything around that feed: getting it into cloud storage, making it watchable live, and building the web application that presents it and ties it to patients and appointments.
problem: The camera feed and its findings stayed on the capture machine, so recordings were not retained centrally and nobody outside the room — family members or dental students — could follow an examination.
solution: Stored the video feed in AWS S3 and added live streaming through AWS IVS, then built a web application that plays back recordings, carries the live stream, and links each session to a patient record and diagnosis.

howItWorks.title: Capture and detection
howItWorks.description: The dentist places a camera-tipped device in the patient's mouth. The C++ application controls the camera, receives the feed, and runs a model that detects caries.

howItWorks.title: Storage and streaming
howItWorks.description: The feed is stored in AWS S3, and AWS IVS carries a live stream so a patient's family or dental students can watch the examination as it happens.

howItWorks.title: Patient-linked sessions
howItWorks.description: A doctor selects a patient in the web application and streams live from the C++ application; the recording is stored against that patient's details automatically.

howItWorks.title: Diagnosis and appointments
howItWorks.description: The doctor writes the diagnosis into the web application, which also handles appointment booking.

buildingProcess.title: Cloud video storage
buildingProcess.description: Added AWS S3 storage for the camera feed coming out of the C++ application.

buildingProcess.title: Live streaming
buildingProcess.description: Added a live streaming feature using AWS IVS so an examination can be watched remotely while it happens.

buildingProcess.title: Web application
buildingProcess.description: Built the web application from scratch to show recorded videos and carry the live stream, with AWS Cognito authentication, appointment booking, and diagnosis entry.

challenges.challenge: A live examination had to end up as a stored recording attached to the right patient, without adding manual filing steps for the dentist.
challenges.solution: Tied the flow together through the web application: the doctor picks the patient first, then streams from the C++ application, and the recording is stored with that patient's details automatically.
challenges.lesson: Choosing where the workflow starts can remove a whole class of manual data entry later.

features: Cloud storage of the intraoral camera feed in AWS S3
Live streaming of examinations through AWS IVS
Video library and live stream playback in the web application
highlights: Added AWS S3 storage and AWS IVS live streaming for an intraoral camera feed driven by a C++ application.
Built the accompanying web application from scratch, with AWS Cognito authentication, appointment booking, and diagnosis entry.
Connected live capture to patient records so streamed examinations are stored against the right patient automatically.
lessonsLearned: How to bridge a native desktop application and a web application through cloud video services.
How live streaming changes what a clinical tool can be used for, including teaching and family visibility.
